name: Fagani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands Languages: An Internal Classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Wordlists 85 Faghani, 86 Rihu'a, 87 Agufi and POC reflex tables; p. 80 footnote notes Pawley (1972) recorded POC *p as /f/ in Faghani from 1920s data, now /h/. The only 'unstressed' mentions are conditioning notes in the reflex tables; no statement of where Fagani word stress falls.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. Solomon Islands field notes, PARADISEC collection AC2 (series other than SISC), 1920s-1970s.
sources.note: Wikipedia claims AC2 holds open-access Fagani materials; only the SISC reprint series was verifiable through OAI, and the catalogue search by language code was could not be reached by automated download; unpublished notes might carry stress marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record faga1239 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: Dialects Agufi, Nuclear Fagani, Rihu'a; most extensive descriptions are both 'a wordlist or less' (Codrington 1885; Tryon & Hackman 1983); no descriptive references.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue page for faf (Dec 2024, Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Only three resources: PARADISEC AC2-SISC101 (primary text), Glottolog, Ethnologue. No language description listed.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 19th ed. (2016), 'Fagani: a language of Solomon Islands' (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: 900 speakers (1999 SIL), NW Makira; dialects Fagani, Rihu'a, Agufi; 'Language Development: Grammar' (unspecified); 'Separate from Arosi (Tryon 1982)'. No phonology.

sources.citation: Lynch, J., M. Ross & T. Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon. Appendix language list p. 885.
sources.note: Lists 'Faghani' between Arosi [this volume] and Bauro with no description cited; no sketch of Fagani in the volume.

sources.citation: Ray, S. H. 1926. A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge: CUP. pp. 470-471 notes on San Cristoval languages.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Comparative survey that summarises Codrington's San Cristoval sketches and occasionally adds phonetic remarks; the baur1252 check could not open it (HathiTrust uc1.32106012047491 could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Codrington, R. H. 1885. The Melanesian Languages. Oxford: Clarendon Press. Ch. 26 'San Cristoval, Fagani', pp. 499-505.
sources.note: Alphabet section (pp. 499-500) lists vowels a e i o u, diphthongs au ao ae ai, consonants k g t p b w f q(=bw) m mw n ng r s and sound correspondences with Wango; the whole chapter (pp. 499-505: alphabet, articles, nouns, pronouns, possessives, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, numerals) says nothing about accent or stress. The volume's only accent remarks are for Mota (p. 253), Florida/Nggela (p. 523) and Bugotu (p. 546).

sources.citation: Ethnologue 'Language Development: Grammar' entry for Fagani (SIL; unspecified work).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Ethnologue's Fagani page records that a grammar exists but does not name it; may just be Codrington 1885 ch. 26, but worth resolving through the Ethnologue bibliography or SIL Solomon Islands.

sources.citation: Pawley, A. 1972. On the internal relationships of Eastern Oceanic languages. In R. C. Green & M. Kelly (eds), Studies in Oceanic Culture History 3, 1-142. Pacific Anthropological Records 13. Honolulu: Bishop Museum.

sources.note: Comparative study that used 1920s Faghani data (per Tryon & Hackman 1983 p. 80 fn.); the source of that data (possibly Capell or Fox notes) may be named there and might be a phonological description.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. 1919. Social Organization in San Cristoval, Solomon Islands. JRAI 49: 94-179.

sources.note: Glottolog's only other Fagani-tagged overview; contains vocabulary and identifies the three San Cristoval language divisions; unlikely but possible phonetic note.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. & F. H. Drew. 1915. Beliefs and tales of San Cristoval (Solomon Islands). Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 45: 131-185, 187-228. (Paradisec AC2-SISC101 typescript/reprint.)

sources.note: Only known published texts in the Fagani, Rihu'a and Agufi dialects; a phonetic/orthographic preface might carry an accent note, and the texts are the only raw Fagani data beyond wordlists.
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

sources.citation: PARADISEC, Arthur Capell collection AC2, series SISC (San Cristoval): AC2-SISC101 Fox & Drew 1915 'Beliefs and tales of San Cristoval' (JRAI 45: 131-228) reprint; AC2-SISC102 Fox 1919 'Social organisation in San Cristoval' reprint with Capell annotations; AC2-SISCRC101 Fox, 'The San Cristoval Heo', JPS 28(1): 39-41.
